ratings.comment: Worst teacher I've ever had in my life.The fact that Sonoma State allows him to be a part of their faculty makes me question their intentions as well.Assignments, quizzes and exams often contain problems which were not discussed in class.Grading is extremely unreasonable as well.Clearly this professor does not care about the success of his students

I was terrified of this class before taking it, but it turned out to be an enjoyable class. He completely restructured the class from Fall 2022. It's very standard: a short quiz every other week, two midterms, and a final. HW is multiple choice with unlimited attempts. Do the practice quiz/exams and you'll pass.

Absolutely the worst CS professor I've ever had. Some of the most inapplicable assignments I've ever seen and will never use. Claims concepts are "simple", but the exams are unnecessarily brutal with a 40ish% avg. Regarding knowledge, you'll get the same result even if you don't attend lectures. This was online. Offline may be different.

Worst teacher I ever had.

He skips over important information during lecture. Hw has questions he has never gone over. On his exams he will take points off for not doing the same work he did, even if your work and answer were correct. He insists on using formal notation while teaching new topics while not explaining what the formal notation means.

First of all his his lectures are completely dry and uninformative. His homework/projects/exam were all filled with multiple errors and confusing directions. Prepare for vague answers on piazza that he takes forever in responding too.
ratings.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

ratings.comment: Probably the worst CS professor you can take at SSU. Inaccurate grading between students, lack of communication, boring lecturer, condescending, unprepared, deviates from syllabus, excessive workload, hands out hw assignments after finals! Avoid at all costs.

Horrible. Absolutely horrible. Constantly claims concepts are "simple" when they're not. Constantly deviates from the syllabus and refuses to address it when anyone brings it up. Projects are practically useless and not relevant to any modern industry work. Tests are unnecessarily hard. Students are expected to use their weekend to take quizzes

I expected to hate 454 and it turned out to be my favorite at SSU. It's tough but very doable. I HIGHLY recommend you get both books Ravi recs. He moves through the material very quickly but he follows the books closely. Sipser's book is actually quite pleasant to read and I hate reading textbooks. Ask questions in OH or on Piazza. He's very nice.

1 of the worst teachers at the school imo. He is hard to understand, doesn't explain things well, skims over difficult topics claiming they are simple. He gets frustrated when students don't understand. His tests are stupid hard. He tests on stuff that is way above the level of his explanation during classes if its even the same material he showed.
ratings.ratingTags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

ratings.comment: His labs are a bit sloppy and the midterm, final, and lab final are all worth like 70% of the course grade.
ratings.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

ratings.comment: Great guy who explains material well. Wants you to succeed and will always help. Daily group quiz, 4 HWs, 3 projects, 2 exams and a final. HW/exams can get difficult projects are not so bad. Biggest complaint is lack of communication and clarity. Takes long time to post grades so you cant verify things are correct. Must always be on his case.

Lectures can drag a bit but Ravi overall knows his stuff and presents material well. It's an algorithms class so, it will require thinking hard about tough concepts but once it clicks, you can appreciate how amazing they are. The projects aren't bad but some HW is quite tough, as are the tests. Take notes, ask questions, and study! No slacking!
ratings.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

ratings.comment: Daily quiz, gives question ahead of time. 2 projects. Final project topics were very difficult to understand/implement. 2 exams and 1 final. Gives solutions to all previous exams and even re-uses questions so study them. Uses Gradiance (multiple choice) for HW, only 6 or 7 HWs. Very nice guy and good instructor but the material is dense/boring/dry

I've taken Ravi for multiple CS courses and try to avoid it. It seems like he learns the topics he is covering as he goes through the lecture. The tests are difficult and worded in a way that makes sense to few students. Teaching yourself the topics through videos/books works better than lecture.
ratings.ratingTags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

ratings.comment: Ravi is an extremely knowledgeable professor, and he tries his best to provide extra study material and help when he can, but his lectures are sometimes difficult to understand. The work is doable, but you will need to spend some time outside of class studying and practicing.
ratings.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

ratings.comment: Ravi is extremely passionate about computer science and mathematics. His lectures are great, but the concepts are hard so it will require a lot of studying outside of class. Tests are hard, but if you go into office hours he will prepare you with practice questions which are similar to what is on the exams. Overall a very intelligent and nice man.

He really seems like a genuine, nice guy. But I learned more from my classmates than I ever did with him this semester. It could be because this material is hard to grasp in general, but I did not enjoy the class.

Very hard class, very good teacher. To do well you must spend a lot of time outside of class either studying or coding up the material. Midterms were very hard; usually 2-3 A's, 4-5 B's, 5 or so C's, and 20-25 D's and F's. Definitely would recommend taking this class during a light semester.

Glosses over extremely difficult topics. Assigns videos instead of teaching, the videos are almost as awful as he is. Ravi writes tests in the most puzzling way possible, expecting you to apply knowledge may not have learned in previous classes. Assigns excessively difficult homework based more on number puzzles than the material. should be fired.

Great professor for this class. He really expects you to have learned linear algebra, discrete math, and probability theory,(all the courses you should have taken by now) and be ready to apply your knowledge. Work through the practice exams and find another programming book that deals with recursion to use as a resource and you'll be set.

Great instructor but it doesn't matter who teaches it, this will require A LOT of effort and studying. If you want an A, you have to read the book and do as many pronblems as possible because Ravi will expect you to master everything. Midterms are extremely rigorous and have two parts: closed book and open book. Open book 10^6x more difficult.

Very kind but challenging teacher. Much of his lectures are spent by him discussing difficult and hardly related topics. He is very smart, though, and you will learn lots if you go into his office hours.

Ravi is one of the most helpful teachers I know. If you express interest and talk with him you will have a much better experience. Go to him for help and he will. Go to every class and lab. Some portions of the class are very dry, but its stuff we need to get through! Tests are HARD, labs are doable, but work. A lot of fun!
Really nice but hard to understand sometimes. He will help you if you ask, but other than that he doesn't engage much with the students.

Really nice guy. However, I was extremely unsure of my grade throughout the whole course. Sometimes goes on tangents during lectures. Tests are really tough and we never had enough time to complete them. Gave us 4 hours for the final -not a single person finished. Definitely learned a lot. Extreme favoritism toward grad students.

Dr Ravikumar is a great professor who takes a lot of interest in his students.  He does expect a lot of his students, but as in most things in life, the hard work pays off.  I definitely recommend taking his courses.

Great professor, very smart, very helpful.  For the Data Mining class, the content is difficult, but Dr Ravikumar goes the extra mile to be accomodating.  His tests can be like an IQ test, but you will learn a lot.  One of my favorites of all time; take any class he offers.  Note that grad students have a far more favorable opinion...

Ravi is an un-teacher by this I mean topics I had a firm understanding of before now make no sense at all.  If you are lucky on his tests one question will actually be something he went over in class.  Expect him not to show up for scheduled office hours.  Any good reviews about this man make me wonder how much he paid them to write those reviews.

It seems like Ravi is really not interested in teaching CS classes.  He doesn't care when the vast majority of his students don't know what he is talking about.  In his own little world.  Seems like he only cares about his CES classes.

Great professor, very talented, very smart.  Keenly interested in his students and his field of work.  Dr Ravikumar more than goes the extra mile for his students.   Take anything he teaches - he's that good.
Nice guy. Very Bright. Couldn't teach a rock to stand still. Rambles about stuff only he understands. Makes more mistakes then his students. Can't pass his own tests. WORST TEACHER EVER.

Very competent, very bright, very engaged, enjoys the subject.  He is very helpful, even coming in to help tutor on weekends!  The CES 512 class is not easy, but that's because the subject is itself is hard.  He's also fair about late assignments and second chances.
Always willing to help eventhough he is super busy.
terrible teacher. babbles in class about nothing. do anything to avoid taking his class. he is a ****!
Yeah, I like signing up for one lab a week and then attending two.
Ravi is very cool and allocates time to help anyone who needs it
Turing machines rule the world
Hard but covers the material.. fair grader after adjusting grades
